title: Aggrega Catalog (Component)
description: The abstract definition of an atomic building block.

version.description: Strict Semantic Versioning of the interface (e.g., 1.0.0).

description.description: A concise, one-sentence summary of what the entity does.

maintainers.description: List of maintainers who own this entity.

repository.description: The URL to the Git repository where the source files live.

home.description: The URL of this entity's home page, wiki, or documentation.

keywords.description: A list of descriptive keywords for UI discoverability.

deprecated.description: Indicates whether this entity is deprecated and should no longer be used.

labels.description: Duck-typing labels to declare characteristics. Must include the reserved 'component.aggrega.ai/type' key.

annotations.description: Immutable, intrinsic component characteristics authored by the Platform Architect in Domain 2. Cascades down to the .context.annotations.catalog bucket.

spec.description: Validation and schema definitions governing the developer's opaque values payload.

extends.description: URI of a base Component to inherit YAML metadata from and auto-merge JSON Schema 2020-12 declarations with.

featuresSchema.description: Declarative attachment slot definitions: the named binding points at which this entity expects a Feature to be attached. A slot constrains which fill may bind it (selector) and how the fill's material may be delivered (inject); the fill's own Feature owns its values and infra contract. Declaring a slot never closes the attachment block — a deployment may attach a Feature under a name no slot declares, so one entity serves both a slot-filled attachment and a credential shared at a broader scope. A slot is a binding point, not a dependency socket: usesSchema declares the separate topology surface.

required.description: Declares that the slot must end up bound. The build halts when no attachment binds the slot's name on an instance of this entity, tested against the attachment set the instance holds after the whole attachment cascade — so an attachment declared at a scope the instance inherits from satisfies the slot exactly as a fill authored on the instance itself does.

inject.description: Allowed inject mechanisms for the slot's material. Empty array = blackbox (the Recipe controls delivery internally and the material is never delivered to the workload).

description.description: Human documentation for this attachment slot.

sensitive.description: Declares that the material this slot carries is sensitive. A declaration only: no compiler behavior reads it today, so setting it changes nothing about validation, rendering, or emitted output.

selector.description: Optional Kubernetes-style label selector constraining which Feature may fill this slot — the slot analog of a usesSchema socket's selector, evaluated against the attached Feature's own labels. A fill whose labels do not satisfy it halts. Omit to place no constraint on the fill.

inject.description: Allowlisted self-inject delivery mechanisms (e.g., ['env', 'file', 'arg']). When present, developers may use the inject: block at the component level in the Aggregate to inject their own values or provides keys directly into the delivery pipe. If omitted, component-level self-inject is forbidden (Black-Box pattern — the Recipe handles all internal wiring). Same semantics as usesSchema[].inject but governs the component's own values rather than cross-component topology.

usesSchema.description: Native YAML schema defining the topology. The Go CLI natively reads this to validate selectors and allowed inject paradigms.

selector.description: Kubernetes-style selector evaluated natively by the Go compiler in Step 4 to guarantee Cross-Node Type Safety before Wasm execution.

inject.description: Allowlisted delivery contracts (e.g., ['env', 'file']). If omitted, delivery dictation is banned (Black-Box pattern).

required.description: When true, developer must declare at least one dependency in this socket.

valueSchema.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 content defining the per-connection value contract for this socket — the developer-supplied values an Aggregate edge may carry into the consuming node's render context. Accepts the same three authoring modes as the Component schema field via content-shape dispatch: inline content, single-file replacement via {$import: <path>}, or cross-document reference via {$ref: <Library>#/schemas/<name>}. Per-edge values are validated against this contract by the Step-1 conformance gate, not structurally at the edge.

infraSchema.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 content defining the per-connection infra contract for this socket — the operator-supplied infra a Release edge may carry. Accepts the same three authoring modes as the Component schema field via content-shape dispatch: inline content, {$import: <path>}, or {$ref: <Library>#/schemas/<name>}. Per-edge infra is validated against this contract by the Step-1 conformance gate.

schema.description: JSON Schema 2020-12 content covering the free-form pillars: values (the Developer's domain — application-shape parameters the Developer configures per Component instance in the Aggregate); infra (the Operator's domain — physical sizing knobs supplied by the Release); and provides (downstream context keys this Component exposes to consumers via the topology pipe). Accepts three authoring modes via content-shape dispatch: (1) inline content (a YAML map carrying compact form, JSON Schema YAML, or mixed); (2) single-file replacement via {$import: <path>}; (3) cross-document reference via {$ref: <Library>#/schemas/<name>} into a SchemaLibrary entry by bare-name identity (the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile; no registry host appears in the reference). The companion fields usesSchema and featuresSchema cover the fixed-shape pillars (dependency sockets, attachment slots); the bridge synthesis composes the three into the entity's unified validation surface.

assertions.description: Build-time cross-field validation. Each entry is a named assertion: the key is a stable rule identifier surfaced in error messages; the value is a Go template string with `{{ fail "message" }}` halt semantics. Multiple named assertions per entity evaluate per-instance in author-declared order; the first failing assertion halts the build. Component assertions evaluate at Step 4b (post-resolution, post-analyzer-gate, pre-render) and express architectural invariants of the contract that hold regardless of which Recipe binds. Template context: .values / .infra / .uses / .features / .metadata. The evaluator uses missingkey=error: references to undefined keys halt with a no-such-key diagnostic. Because the bare reference halts before any fallback can run, a plain `default` does not supply an optional-field fallback on this surface — gate the reference with `hasKey`, or read it through `index` and then apply `default`, or use the `optional` helper, which performs the presence check directly.
